# Your first swarm

Two agents editing one repo, zero checkouts, one prevented conflict.
By the end you'll have claimed a resource before touching it,
landed ops as ordinary commits, and pushed the coordination layer
to the remote — the whole sturn loop.

## Install

The `sturn` command ships as a [tamias](https://9aia.com/tamias/)
pack — a generated shim over `tamias-driver-sturn`. With tamias:

```sh
tamias install 9aia:sturn@<version>          # org registry
# or from a checkout:
tamias install --allow-drivers ./libraries/sturn
```

A compat `sturn` bin also exists in `sturn-cli`, so a plain
`cargo install --git https://github.com/9aia/sturn sturn` works too.

## Set up a repo

```sh
git init demo && cd demo
git commit -qm init --allow-empty
sturn init            # writes sturn.toml, confirms ref namespaces
sturn daemon &        # WAL → repo.<id>.{ops,claims,…}; or:
sturn deploy service  # systemd user unit, Restart=always
```

`sturn init` also detects colocated jj repos — sturn works on them
unchanged. You should see `wrote sturn.toml` (or an unchanged
report) and the daemon logging topic fan-out.

## Two workspaces

Workspaces are pointers, not checkouts — `refs/sturn/ws/<name>` is
a ref to a commit:

```sh
sturn ws new agent-a
sturn ws new agent-b
sturn ws ls            # both point at HEAD; nothing hit disk
```

## Claim before you edit

Claims publish advisory locks *before* edits — that's the whole
point:

```sh
STURN_ACTOR=agent-a sturn claim "src/**" --ws agent-a
# claimed src/** (ws agent-a, ttl 3600s)

STURN_ACTOR=agent-b sturn claim "src/lib.rs" --ws agent-b
# conflict: agent-a claimed src/** (ws agent-a, expires …)
# sturn: claim denied — --force to override
```

Agent-b learns in milliseconds that `src/` is taken and picks
`tests/**` instead. In git, both would have edited the file and
discovered it at merge. `sturn check "src/lib.rs"` probes the same
conflict set without claiming; `--fence` asks "has my claim been
superseded?"

## Write ops, snap, push

Ops are the only write path — `write` content becomes an ODB blob:

```sh
echo 'fn helper() { 42 }' | STURN_ACTOR=agent-a sturn write src/lib.rs --ws agent-a --intent "add helper"
echo '…' | STURN_ACTOR=agent-b sturn write tests/lib.rs --ws agent-b
echo '…' | STURN_ACTOR=agent-b sturn rename tests/lib.rs tests/helper.rs --ws agent-b
sturn log --ws agent-a    # JSONL replay of the WAL
```

`snap` folds a workspace's ops into a real commit — several ws
merge into ONE commit, rename-aware:

```sh
sturn snap agent-a -m "a: lib"   # → ordinary commit on main
sturn snap agent-b -m "b: test" # → ordinary commit on main
git log --oneline                # two normal commits
```

Then publish heads *and* the coordination layer:

```sh
sturn push    # heads + refs/sturn/* → origin
```

## What you now know

* The WAL (`refs/sturn/wal/*`) is the state; the bus and workspaces
  are rebuildable caches — the daemon only removes latency.
* Claims prevent collisions; `snap` is the only thing that becomes
  a commit; merges stay git's.
* `STURN_ACTOR` names who you are on the ops you append.

## Go deeper

* [Hydrate a workspace](../how-to/hydrate.md) — materialize the ws
  view for compilers that need POSIX files.
* [Mount a workspace](../how-to/mount.md) — FUSE: tools write
  normally, sturn records ops.
* [Run the daemon](../how-to/daemon.md) — service lifecycle.
* [Architecture](../explanation/architecture.md) — the three-layer
  model and its invariants.
* [The model](../explanation/model.md) — virtual files, per-op
  approval, agents reviewing agents.
* [Reference: ops](../reference/ops.md) — the full op vocabulary.

url: /sturn/how-to/hydrate.md

# Hydrate a workspace

Agents read through the ODB; compilers need POSIX files. Hydration
materializes the ws *view* — tip commit **plus** uncommitted WAL
ops, matching what `ws_read` sees.

```sh
sturn ws hydrate agent-7 /tmp/ws-7            # whole view
sturn ws hydrate agent-7 /tmp/ws-7 --path src # subset
```

Or hydrate + run + clean in one step:

```sh
sturn exec --ws agent-7 -- cargo check        # tmpfs, gone after
sturn exec --ws agent-7 --keep -- cargo test  # keep the dir
```

* Target tmpfs (`/dev/shm`/`/tmp`) — it's a projection, delete freely.
* Exit status propagates: `sturn exec` fails iff the command does.
* Writes inside the hydrated dir flow back as ops only with
  `--writeback` (`sturn exec --ws <w> --writeback -- cmd` or
  `sturn ws hydrate <w> <dir> --writeback`) — a post-run dir diff
  becomes Write/Delete/Rename ops. Without it, ops remain the only
  write path.
* FUSE mounts for humans: `sturn mount <w> <dir> --rw` — see
  [mount](mount.md).

---

---
url: /sturn/how-to/mount.md
---
# How-to: mount a workspace

`sturn mount` exposes a workspace tree as a real filesystem — the
interception layer: tools write normally, sturn records ops.

```
agent's write_file() ──► kernel ──► FUSE ──► SturnFs
                                          write() → buffer
                                          release → Op::Write → WAL
```

FUSE = *Filesystem in USErspace*: syscalls route to a user process
instead of a disk driver, so `sturn-fuse` decides what "a file"
means — ops, not bytes on disk.

## Use

```console
$ sturn mount devin /mnt/devin        # read-only view of the tree
$ sturn mount --rw devin /mnt/devin   # writes become WAL ops
```

Under `--rw`, plain POSIX writes — `echo`, editors, build tools,
agent `write_file` — land as `Write`/`Rename`/`Delete` ops with
`intent: "fuse"`. The agent can't bypass the write path: it *is* a
filesystem, the thing tools already use.

## Semantics

* **Buffer-then-commit**: `write()` buffers per open file; the op
  emits on `release` (close) or `fsync` — editors that fsync-per-
  save get an op at sync point, not just at close.
* **Mount-time view**: the tree is the ws tip at mount time —
  other agents' ops don't appear live (unmount/remount to see).
* **Dirs are implicit** in git trees — `mkdir`/`rmdir` are local
  only; a `Write` op into the dir is what persists.

```console
$ fusermount -u /mnt/devin
```

url: /sturn/how-to/daemon.md
---
# Run the daemon

`sturn daemon` polls WAL heads and fans new events onto topics
(`repo.<id>.ops|claims|review|presence`) in the embedded bus store.

```sh
sturn daemon                      # foreground
sturn deploy service              # systemd user unit, Restart=always
sturn service disable             # stop now + skip at login (unit kept)
sturn service enable              # back on, now and at login
sturn service status              # enabled=/active= probe
sturn service restart             # bounce in place
sturn service logs -f             # journal tail; -f follows
sturn destroy service             # disable + remove the unit file
```

## If the daemon is down

Nothing is lost. The bus is a cache — ops still live in
`refs/sturn/wal/*` and replicate via `git push`/`git fetch`.
Subscribers catch up by replaying the WAL. The daemon only removes
latency; it never owns truth.

## Consumers today

* `sturn claims` — fold all WALs into live advisory locks
* M2: SSE/unix-socket subscribers; M3: the MCP `subs` tool

---

---
url: /sturn/explanation/architecture.md
---
# Architecture

Three layers, strictly ordered by authority:

```
        ┌────────── evented layer ──────────┐
agents  │  ops: write/rename/claim/intent/… │
        │  virtual workspaces (ws = pointer) │
        │  bus: repo.<id>.{ops,claims,…}     │
        └──────┬─────────────────┬───────────┘
               │ append          │ append (offline)
        refs/sturn/wal/* ── git ODB ── refs/sturn/ws/*
               │
        normal git push/fetch → GitHub — free, signed, ordinary
```

## Invariants

1. **The WAL is the state.** Anything derivable from
   `refs/sturn/wal/*` is a cache (bus cursors, materialized views).
2. **Merges stay git's.** Ops never encode merge semantics — claims
   prevent collisions; `snap` squashes into ordinary commits.
3. **Coordination before work.** Claims publish *before* edits.
   Discovering a conflict at merge is the failure mode git taught us.

## What each piece owes

* `refs/sturn/wal/<ws>` — source of truth, replicates for free
* daemon + bus — latency reduction only; optional
* `refs/sturn/ws/<name>` — workspace namespaces; hydration opt-in
* `snap` — the bridge back to ordinary git history

See [Boundaries](boundaries.md) for owns / doesn't-own.

## Where it sits

In the org's layering — **tamias** (package & content manager) →
**engines** (myco records, kuda code maps, mimus proofs, sepia
sessions, hypha substrate, tarsi releases, cicada schedules, cypera
docs, scarab config) → **orchestration** (peregrin campaigns) →
**surfaces** (pavo views, MCP fronts, agent harnesses).

Sturn is an **engine** — the coordination substrate every agent
calls directly, below orchestration. It isn't orchestrated itself:
agents `claim`/`write`/`snap` against the WAL, the daemon only
fans events onto topics, and peregrin campaigns can consume sturn
ops as events without sturn knowing they exist.

---

---
url: /sturn/explanation/boundaries.md
---
# Boundaries

Sturn owns **ephemeral coordination** — live claims, ops, topics,
asks over VCS state. Neighbors own theirs:

* **myco** — durable work memory (the `project/` ledger); sturn
  coordinates the moment, myco remembers the intent.
* **kuda** — code memory; `.kuda/` cards are that repo's concern.
* **tamias** — distribution; the `sturn` command is a tamias pack,
  releases run through `tarsi-serve`.
* **peregrin/hypha** — orchestration substrate; sturn is the
  coordination layer agents call directly.

---

---
url: /sturn/explanation/concepts.md
---
# Concepts

The domain vocabulary, each term defined once. The op-level
contract lives in [Reference: ops](../reference/ops).

## WAL (write-ahead log)

`refs/sturn/wal/<ws>` — the append-only op log per workspace, stored
as ordinary git objects. **The WAL is the state**: anything
derivable from it (bus cursors, materialized views, live claims) is
a rebuildable cache.

## Op

The unit of coordination: `write`, `rename`, `delete`, `claim`,
`release`, `intent`, `review`, `ask`/`answer`, `presence`. Ops are
metadata about work — they never encode merge semantics. Content
payloads become ODB blobs; ops reference them.

## Workspace (`ws`)

A named pointer — `refs/sturn/ws/<name>` → a commit — plus that
workspace's WAL. Zero materialization: no clone, no worktree, no
checkout. `sturn ws new` costs a ref.

## Claim

An advisory lock on a resource URI (`fs:src/**`, `dev:display0`,
`sess:T-012`) published *before* edits, with a TTL. Conflicts are
learned in milliseconds on the claims topic — prevention, not
merge-time discovery. `sturn check` probes the conflict set;
`--fence` asks whether your claim was superseded.

## Topic / bus

`repo.<id>.{ops,claims,review,presence,asks}` — the pub/sub cache
the daemon fans WAL events onto. **A cache, never authority**: when
the daemon is down, ops still sync through git push/fetch and
subscribers replay the WAL.

## Snap

The bridge back to ordinary git: folds a workspace's ops into a
real commit on the branch. Multiple workspaces merge into ONE
commit — rename-aware, semantic conflicts warn and later ops win.

## Review / ask

`review <op-id> approve|reject` is itself an attributed op —
per-op approval that streams *before* commit time. `[review]
require = true` makes `snap` refuse unreviewed ops. `ask` opens a
pending-response question any actor may answer; `wait` blocks on
the verdict.

## Actor

Who you are on the ops you append — `STURN_ACTOR` env or config.
Every op is attributed and (optionally) signed; `sturn verify`
checks signatures against `allowed_signers`.

## Hydrate / mount / exec

The three ways to get real files: `ws hydrate`/`exec` materialize
the ws *view* (tip + uncommitted ops) to a dir/tmpfs;
`sturn mount --rw` exposes it as a FUSE filesystem where POSIX
writes become ops. See [model](model.md).

---

---
url: /sturn/explanation/decisions.md
---
# Decisions

ADR-lite: the load-bearing decisions, each with the alternative it
beat and the consequence it carries. Design history lives in the
`project/` myco ledger.

## The WAL is the state

**Decision:** ops live in `refs/sturn/wal/*` as ordinary git
objects; the bus, cursors, and materialized views are caches.

* *Alternative:* a dedicated database (or the bus) as authority.
* *Consequence:* replication is plain `git push`/`fetch` — signed
  by git's machinery, no new sync protocol. Cost: everything
  reconstructible must *stay* reconstructible; the rule is
  enforced by review.

## Ops are metadata; merges stay git's

**Decision:** coordination ops never encode merge semantics —
claims prevent collisions, `snap` produces ordinary commits.

* *Alternative:* CRDT merge for the tree, or a custom merge driver.
* *Consequence:* see [Why no CRDT for code](no-crdt.md) — the log
  converges deterministically, the tree needs decisions, and
  claims make most collisions never happen.

## Workspaces are pointers

**Decision:** `refs/sturn/ws/<name>` is a ref, not a checkout — a
thousand agent workspaces cost nothing.

* *Alternative:* git worktrees or clones per agent.
* *Consequence:* parallelism scales to the ref namespace; real
  files materialize only on demand (hydrate/exec/mount) for the
  tools that genuinely need POSIX.

## Claims before edits

**Decision:** advisory locks publish *before* work starts —
coordination precedes the edit, not the merge.

* *Alternative:* detect conflicts at merge/snap time.
* *Consequence:* contenders learn in milliseconds and pick
  different resources; the failure mode git taught us (discovering
  the collision at a three-way merge) is designed out.

## Continuous review over the PR gate

**Decision:** every op streams through the WAL and can carry a
`review` verdict; `[review] require` gates `snap` per-op.

* *Alternative:* one big diff reviewed at PR time.
* *Consequence:* verdicts land *before* commit time, per op, from
  any actor (agents review agents); PRs become packaging, not the
  gate.

---

---
url: /sturn/explanation/no-crdt.md
---
# Why no CRDT for code

CRDTs are right for the *log*, wrong for the *tree*.

**For the WAL:** when replicas append ops and diverge, a CRDT-style
merge (grow-only set + causal order) converges the log with no
coordination — same events, same state. That part we keep.

**For the tree:** a CRDT auto-merge produces a *syntactically*
merged file, not a semantically correct one. Two agents inserting
different `main()` bodies converge to a file that compiles only by
luck. Code needs decisions, not convergence.

So sturn splits the difference:

* The **log** merges deterministically (CRDT semantics; a
  `libgrite-git` impl is on the backlog).
* The **tree** is produced by `snap` — a deterministic reduction
  over ops on a base. When ops collide semantically, that's a
  decision for a reviewer, not a merge algorithm.
* **Claims** make most collisions never happen — prevention beats
  resolution.

---

---
url: /sturn/explanation/model.md
---
# The model — files, approval, agents

## Files are a projection, not the state

Git materializes a working tree because POSIX tools need paths.
Sturn keeps the tree *virtual*: `ws_read` serves blob contents
straight from the object database — no checkout, no index, no lock.

When something genuinely needs real files:

* `sturn exec --ws w -- cmd` — hydrate the ws view (tip +
  uncommitted ops) to tmpfs, run, discard
* `sturn mount w /dir --rw` — live FUSE filesystem; edits buffer
  per-open and become Write/Delete/Rename ops on release
* `--writeback` on `exec`/`hydrate` — dir diffs flow back as ops

Agents aren't filesystem-deprived — `ws_read/ws_write/ws_glob/
ws_grep` are the same file primitives harnesses already use; the
backend is virtualized, not the interaction.

## Approval without the PR cliff

Every op is content-addressed and streams through the WAL. A
reviewer emits `review <op-id> approve|reject` — itself a signed,
attributed op. With `[review] require = true`, `snap` refuses
unreviewed tree ops and names their ids — the gate exists, but
verdicts stream *per-op before commit time* instead of one giant
diff at the end. PRs become a packaging format, not the gate.

## Agents review agents

A verdict is just an op — any actor appends it. Intended topology:
fast writers produce ops → a senior agent or human watches `subs
ops|review` and emits verdicts → gated `snap` lands only approved
work. Humans spot-check the stream instead of serializing merges.

---

---
url: /sturn/reference/ops.md
---
# Ops

The event vocabulary appended to `refs/sturn/wal/<ws>`. JSON,
content-addressed (blob sha = event id), one commit per append.

## Tree ops

| Op | Fields | Effect at `snap` |
|---|---|---|
| `write` | `path`, `blob`, `intent?` | replace/create file |
| `rename` | `from`, `to` | move entry |
| `delete` | `path` | remove entry |

## Multi-workspace merge

`sturn snap a b …` folds several workspaces' pending ops into one
commit — rename-aware, not a bare path concat:

* a `write` onto a path *another* ws renamed away follows the
  rename to its destination (the modify-vs-rename case a 3-way
  merge resolves the same way), chained f→g→h and applied after
  the rename no matter the ws order;
* genuinely ambiguous shapes stay put and warn on stderr instead
  of picking a silent winner: a source renamed two ways
  (`rename f diverged`), a `delete` meeting a rename (either
  side), colliding destinations, and cross-ws same-path
  write/delete collisions.

## Coordination ops

| Op | Fields | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `claim` | `glob`, `ttl_secs` | advisory lock; auto-expires |
| `release` | `glob` | drop a claim |
| `intent` | `text` | provenance — why the work exists |
| `review` | `event`, `verdict` | approve/reject an event id |
| `snapshot` | `message` | marker — ops before it are committed |
| `presence` | `status` | actor joined/left |
| `ask` | `subject`, `target`, `options?`, `ttl_secs` | pending *response* — open question; the event id is the ask handle |
| `answer` | `ask`, `verdict` | close an ask with a verdict |
| `cancel` | `ask` | withdraw an open ask |

## Claims

`claim.glob` carries a resource URI — `scheme:path`. `fs:` globs
(`src/**`, and a bare glob means `fs:`) or opaque resources
(`dev:display0`, `sess:T-012`, `cap:role`). `net:` paths may be
port ranges — `net:13000-13100` conflicts with `net:13050`;
non-numeric paths fall back to prefix matching.

Each live claim derives a **fencing token** at fold time — a
Lamport-style epoch: `1 + max` over earlier claims on overlapping
URIs, ordered by `ts` then WAL position. Never stored, and never
repeats for a resource — expired and released claims still count
as predecessors. `sturn claim` prints it; a holder passes it to
`sturn check <uri> --fence <n>` to ask "has anything outranked
me?" — the stale-usurper probe. It's advisory like the claim:
second-granularity `ts` plus concatenation order means
same-second cross-ws races resolve deterministically, not
temporally.

## Asks

Claims are pending *ownership*; asks are pending *answers*. An
`ask` opens under its event id and stays `open` until an `answer`
or `cancel` op lands — or `ttl_secs` runs out (`0` = never). The
question and its answer can live on different workspaces' WALs;
responders filter `target` (`actor:<n>`, `human:<n>`, `node:<h>`,
`claim-holder:<glob>`, `any`) to find asks meant for them.

## Envelope

```json
{"id":"<blob sha>","ws":"agent-7","actor":"agent-7","ts":1792292994,
 "op":{"op":"write","path":"src/lib.rs","blob":"<sha>","intent":"…"}}
```

## `sturn`

Evented coordination over the git object store — agents murmurate, not merge

**Usage:** `sturn [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

###### **Commands:**

* `init` — Wire a repo for sturn — writes sturn.toml if absent
* `ws` — Workspace namespaces — virtual checkouts that cost a pointer
* `claim` — Advisory lock on a resource URI — published *before* edits
* `release` — Drop a claim — same URI form `claim` takes
* `write` — Append a write op — --content, --file, or stdin becomes an ODB blob
* `rename` — Append a rename op — intent survives where git loses it
* `delete` — Append a delete op
* `intent` — Record why work exists — provenance as data
* `compact` — Drop pre-snapshot WAL history (archived, not lost)
* `log` — Replay the WAL — ops in order, JSONL. `--topic`/`--limit` filter the stream; `--wait-ms` long-polls (bounded) for new events before printing — the daemon-free `subs` pull
* `diff` — In-flight ops per workspace — logged since the last snap, not yet landed. `--live` keeps streaming as new ops arrive
* `snap` — Fold ws ops into a real commit on the branch. Multiple ws = merged into ONE commit — rename-aware (writes follow renames); semantic conflicts warn on stderr, later ops win same-path
* `review` — Approve/reject an event — continuous review
* `push` — Push heads + refs/sturn/\* — coordination rides the remote
* `daemon` — WAL→topic fan-out loop. The bus is a cache — ops still sync through git when it's down
* `sub` — Stream a topic live — ops|claims|review|presence, JSONL
* `join` — Announce presence — `leave` drops all the actor's claims
* `leave` — Leave a ws — sweeps the actor's claims on it
* `verify` — Verify event signatures against allowed_signers
* `claims` — Live claims across every workspace
* `check` — List live claims conflicting with a URI — consult before acting on a resource. Exits 1 when the URI is contested
* `ask` — Open a pending-response ask — the printed event id is the ask handle that `answer`/`cancel`/`wait` take
* `asks` — Pending asks across every workspace — open by default
* `answer` — Answer an open ask — the verdict rides your ws's WAL
* `cancel` — Withdraw an open ask
* `wait` — Block until an ask resolves — prints the result as JSON. Exit: 0 answered, 2 cancelled, 3 expired, 4 timeout. `--timeout 0` (the default) waits until resolved — unbounded; a bare `cli.wait` op can park a request forever, pass `--timeout` for a bounded wait
* `bridge` — Bridge snapshot events to a bupha webhook — GitHub-shaped, HMAC-signed. Bupha runs CI on snaps with zero bupha changes
* `exec` — Hydrate a ws to tmpfs and run a command inside — compilers need POSIX; agents don't. Exits with the command's status
* `mount` — Mount a ws tree via FUSE — POSIX for tools/GUIs. --rw: edits flow back as Write/Delete/Rename ops
* `deploy` — Deploy the daemon — systemd user unit + env skeleton
* `destroy` — Teardown counterparts of `deploy`
* `service` — Toggle the daemon unit without removing it — free the box when fan-out isn't needed, `enable` brings it back

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help
* `-V, --version` — Print version

## `sturn init`

Wire a repo for sturn — writes sturn.toml if absent

**Usage:** `sturn init [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn ws`

Workspace namespaces — virtual checkouts that cost a pointer

**Usage:** `sturn ws [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

###### **Commands:**

* `new` — Create a workspace — zero materialization, just a ref
* `ls` — List workspaces
* `read` — Read a file from a ws — the live view: tip + uncommitted ops, same fold `hydrate` materializes
* `paths` — List paths in a ws tree (tip + pending ops), optionally glob-filtered — `**` lists everything
* `grep` — Substring search across a ws tree (tip + pending ops) — `path:line: text` per hit. `--path` restricts to a glob
* `hydrate` — Materialize a ws tree into a dir — tip + uncommitted ops. --path filters to a subset (repeatable); empty = whole tree

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn ws new`

Create a workspace — zero materialization, just a ref

**Usage:** `sturn ws new [OPTIONS] <NAME>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<NAME>`

###### **Options:**

* `--base <BASE>` — Base commit/branch (default: HEAD)
* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn ws ls`

List workspaces

**Usage:** `sturn ws ls [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn ws read`

Read a file from a ws — the live view: tip + uncommitted ops, same fold `hydrate` materializes

**Usage:** `sturn ws read [OPTIONS] <NAME> <PATH>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<NAME>`
* `<PATH>`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn ws paths`

List paths in a ws tree (tip + pending ops), optionally glob-filtered — `**` lists everything

**Usage:** `sturn ws paths [OPTIONS] <NAME> [PATTERN]`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<NAME>`
* `[PATTERN]` — Glob filter — same grammar claims use

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn ws grep`

Substring search across a ws tree (tip + pending ops) — `path:line: text` per hit. `--path` restricts to a glob

**Usage:** `sturn ws grep [OPTIONS] <NAME> <PATTERN>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<NAME>`
* `<PATTERN>` — Substring to find

###### **Options:**

* `--path <PATH>` — Only search paths matching this glob
* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn ws hydrate`

Materialize a ws tree into a dir — tip + uncommitted ops. --path filters to a subset (repeatable); empty = whole tree

**Usage:** `sturn ws hydrate [OPTIONS] <NAME> <DIR>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<NAME>`
* `<DIR>`

###### **Options:**

* `--path <PATHS>`
* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `--writeback` — After materializing, diff the dir back into ops now
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn claim`

Advisory lock on a resource URI — published *before* edits

**Usage:** `sturn claim [OPTIONS] --ws <WS> <URI>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<URI>` — Resource URI or path glob — "fs:src/\*\*", "dev:display0", "net:13000", "sess:T-012"; a bare glob means "fs:"

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--ws <WS>` — Workspace claiming it
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `--ttl <TTL>` — Seconds the claim lives (auto-expiry, no zombie locks) \[default: 3600]
* `--force` — Take the claim even if it conflicts with a live one
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn release`

Drop a claim — same URI form `claim` takes

**Usage:** `sturn release [OPTIONS] --ws <WS> <URI>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<URI>`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--ws <WS>`
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn write`

Append a write op — --content, --file, or stdin becomes an ODB blob

**Usage:** `sturn write [OPTIONS] --ws <WS> <PATH>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<PATH>` — Path inside the tree

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--ws <WS>`
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `--file <FILE>`
* `--content <CONTENT>` — Inline content — the wire-friendly form (ops pass it as a param; no stdin needed)
* `--intent <INTENT>` — Why this edit exists — attached to the op
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn rename`

Append a rename op — intent survives where git loses it

###### **Arguments:**

###### **Options:**

###### **Options:**

* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn compact`

Drop pre-snapshot WAL history (archived, not lost)

**Usage:** `sturn compact [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--ws <WS>` — One workspace, or all when omitted
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn log`

Replay the WAL — ops in order, JSONL. `--topic`/`--limit` filter the stream; `--wait-ms` long-polls (bounded) for new events before printing — the daemon-free `subs` pull

**Usage:** `sturn log [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--ws <WS>` — One workspace, or all when omitted
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `--topic <TOPIC>` — Restrict to one topic: ops|claims|review|presence|asks
* `--limit <LIMIT>` — Keep only the last N matching events
* `--wait-ms <WAIT_MS>` — Wait up to N ms for new events before printing (0/omitted = snapshot now)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn diff`

In-flight ops per workspace — logged since the last snap, not yet landed. `--live` keeps streaming as new ops arrive

**Usage:** `sturn diff [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--ws <WS>` — One workspace, or all when omitted
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `--json` — Emit the raw events as JSONL (same shape `log` produces)
* `--live` — Keep streaming new ops — WAL poll, works daemon-free
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn snap`

Fold ws ops into a real commit on the branch. Multiple ws = merged into ONE commit — rename-aware (writes follow renames); semantic conflicts warn on stderr, later ops win same-path

**Usage:** `sturn snap [OPTIONS] --message <MESSAGE> <WS>...`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<WS>...`

###### **Options:**

* `-m, --message <MESSAGE>`
* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--branch <BRANCH>` — Branch to update (default: repo.branch / main)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn review`

Approve/reject an event — continuous review

**Usage:** `sturn review [OPTIONS] --ws <WS> <EVENT> <VERDICT>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<EVENT>` — Event id (blob sha) to judge
* `<VERDICT>` — approve | reject

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--ws <WS>`
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn push`

Push heads + refs/sturn/\* — coordination rides the remote

**Usage:** `sturn push [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--remote <REMOTE>` — \[default: origin]
* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn daemon`

WAL→topic fan-out loop. The bus is a cache — ops still sync through git when it's down

**Usage:** `sturn daemon [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)

###### **Options:**

* `-h, --help` — Print help

* `<WS>`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

Leave a ws — sweeps the actor's claims on it

###### **Arguments:**

* `<WS>`

###### **Options:**

## `sturn claims`

Live claims across every workspace

**Usage:** `sturn claims [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn check`

List live claims conflicting with a URI — consult before acting on a resource. Exits 1 when the URI is contested

**Usage:** `sturn check [OPTIONS] <URI>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<URI>` — Resource URI or path glob — same form `claim` takes

###### **Options:**

* `--fence <FENCE>` — Staleness probe: report only conflicting claims with a fencing token above N — pass the fence `claim` printed to ask "has my claim been superseded?"
* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `--watch` — Keep watching — stream conflict-set changes via WAL poll. Works daemon-free; combines with --fence
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn ask`

Open a pending-response ask — the printed event id is the ask handle that `answer`/`cancel`/`wait` take

**Usage:** `sturn ask [OPTIONS] --ws <WS> <SUBJECT>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<SUBJECT>` — What is being asked

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--ws <WS>` — Workspace asking
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `--target <TARGET>` — Who may answer — free-form spec: `actor:<name>`, `human:<name>`, `node:<host>`, `claim-holder:<glob>`, `any` \[default: any]
* `--option <OPTIONS>` — Offered verdict — repeatable, advisory only
* `--ttl <TTL>` — Seconds until the ask expires. 0 = never \[default: 3600]
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn asks`

Pending asks across every workspace — open by default

**Usage:** `sturn asks [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--all` — Include resolved asks (answered/cancelled/expired)
* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `--json` — Emit a JSON array instead of text lines
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn answer`

Answer an open ask — the verdict rides your ws's WAL

**Usage:** `sturn answer [OPTIONS] --ws <WS> <ASK> <VERDICT>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<ASK>` — Ask event id
* `<VERDICT>`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--ws <WS>` — Workspace answering
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn cancel`

Withdraw an open ask

**Usage:** `sturn cancel [OPTIONS] --ws <WS> <ASK>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<ASK>` — Ask event id

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--ws <WS>`
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn wait`

Block until an ask resolves — prints the result as JSON. Exit: 0 answered, 2 cancelled, 3 expired, 4 timeout. `--timeout 0` (the default) waits until resolved — unbounded; a bare `cli.wait` op can park a request forever, pass `--timeout` for a bounded wait

**Usage:** `sturn wait [OPTIONS] <ASK>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<ASK>` — Ask event id

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--timeout <TIMEOUT>` — Max seconds to wait. 0 = until resolved (unbounded — the default) \[default: 0]
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `--poll <POLL>` — Poll interval, ms \[default: 100]
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn bridge`

Bridge snapshot events to a bupha webhook — GitHub-shaped, HMAC-signed. Bupha runs CI on snaps with zero bupha changes

**Usage:** `sturn bridge [OPTIONS] --to <TO>`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--to <TO>` — bupha listener URL (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:29173/)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `--secret-env <SECRET_ENV>` — Env var naming the webhook secret (HMAC-SHA256) \[default: BUPHA_WEBHOOK_SECRET]
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn exec`

Hydrate a ws to tmpfs and run a command inside — compilers need POSIX; agents don't. Exits with the command's status

**Usage:** `sturn exec [OPTIONS] --ws <WS> <CMD>...`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<CMD>...` — Command + args, after `--`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--ws <WS>` — Workspace to hydrate
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `--keep` — Keep the hydrated dir after exit
* `--writeback` — Write filesystem edits back as ops on the ws
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn mount`

Mount a ws tree via FUSE — POSIX for tools/GUIs. --rw: edits flow back as Write/Delete/Rename ops

**Usage:** `sturn mount [OPTIONS] <WS> <DIR>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<WS>`
* `<DIR>`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--rw`
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn deploy`

Deploy the daemon — systemd user unit + env skeleton

**Usage:** `sturn deploy [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

###### **Commands:**

* `service` — Write + enable the systemd user unit for `sturn daemon`
* `env` — Seed ~/.config/sturn/env (0600, names only)

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

Write + enable the systemd user unit for `sturn daemon`

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn deploy env`

Seed ~/.config/sturn/env (0600, names only)

**Usage:** `sturn deploy env [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)

Disable + remove the systemd user unit

## `sturn service`

Toggle the daemon unit without removing it — free the box when fan-out isn't needed, `enable` brings it back

**Usage:** `sturn service [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

###### **Commands:**

* `enable` — Enable + start the daemon unit now and at login
* `disable` — Stop the daemon now; stays stopped across logins until `service enable` (the unit file is kept)
* `status` — Whether the daemon unit is enabled and running
* `restart` — Bounce the daemon unit in place
* `logs` — Recent journal lines — `-f` follows the stream live

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn service enable`

Enable + start the daemon unit now and at login

**Usage:** `sturn service enable [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn service disable`

Stop the daemon now; stays stopped across logins until `service enable` (the unit file is kept)

**Usage:** `sturn service disable [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn service status`

Whether the daemon unit is enabled and running

**Usage:** `sturn service status [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn service restart`

Bounce the daemon unit in place

**Usage:** `sturn service restart [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

## `sturn service logs`

Recent journal lines — `-f` follows the stream live

**Usage:** `sturn service logs [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `-f, --f` — Follow the log stream (journalctl -f)
* `--repo <REPO>` — Repo dir (default: cwd)
* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (default: $STURN_CONFIG → ./sturn.toml → ~/.config/sturn/)
* `-h, --help` — Print help

# Config — `sturn.toml`

## Top level

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `RepoCfg` | required | The coordinated repo. |
| `wal` | `WalCfg` | optional | — |
| `bus` | `BusCfg` | optional | — |
| `actor` | `ActorCfg` | optional | — |
| `signing` | `SigningCfg` | optional | — |
| `review` | `ReviewCfg` | optional | — |
| `hooks` | `HooksCfg` | optional | — |

## `[repo]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dir` | `path` | required | Repo dir (the ODB lives at `&lt;dir&gt;/.git`). |
| `id` | `string` | optional | Topic prefix id, e.g. "9aia/sturn". Defaults to dir basename. |
| `branch` | `string` | optional | Branch `snap` updates by default. |

## `[wal]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ref_prefix` | `string` | optional | WAL ref prefix — one ref per workspace beneath it. |

## `[bus]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `store` | `path` | optional | Embedded store path for the local bus impl. |
| `poll_ms` | `int` | optional | Daemon poll interval for WAL→topic fan-out, ms. |
| `repos` | `list` | optional | Extra repo dirs this daemon also fans out — multi-repo from one process. Topic ids derive from dir basename. |

## `[actor]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | optional | Actor name. Defaults to `$STURN_ACTOR`, then `$USER`. |

## `[signing]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | `string` | optional | Private key path (ed25519). ~ expands. |
| `allowed_signers` | `string` | optional | allowed_signers for `sturn verify`. |

## `[review]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `require` | `bool` | optional | Every Write/Rename/Delete since last snap must hold an Approve review (in any ws's WAL) before `snap` lands. |

## `[hooks]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `post_op` | `list` | optional | Shell commands spawned (`sh -c`, detached, cwd = repo dir) after a successful ref-moving verb — claim, leave, write, snap, push, … The event-driven way to re-index: e.g. `post_op = "kuda sync"` replaces `kuda watch --poll-refs` when sturn drives the writes. One string or a list; `$STURN_POST_OP` (single command) overrides. |

## Constraints

* Search order: `--config <path>` → `$STURN_CONFIG` →
  `./sturn.toml` → `~/.config/sturn/sturn.toml`.
* Every table has `deny_unknown_fields` — typos fail the load.
* Secrets never live here; secret material resolves through the
  `Secrets` chain (`sturn-secret` → keyring/dotenv).
* `[hooks] post_op` also reads `$STURN_POST_OP` (single command
  overrides the configured list).

---

---
url: /sturn/reference/crate-api.md
---
# Crate map

Ports (traits only) and impls — new backends are new impl crates,
never core changes.

| crate | layer | purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `sturn-ask` | domain | pending-response asks: fold ops into open questions and verdicts |
| `sturn-claim` | domain | advisory claims: fold ops into live locks, detect overlap |
| `sturn-core` | domain | domain types: op/event schema, sturn.toml config |
| `sturn-bus` | port | Bus port: topic pub/sub over the WAL (a cache, not authority) |
| `sturn-secret` | port | Secrets port: named-secret resolution |
| `sturn-service` | port | Service port: OS service lifecycle |
| `sturn-wal` | port | Wal port: append-only op log inside git refs |
| `sturn-ws` | port | Ws port: virtual workspaces over the git ODB |
| `sturn-bus-redb` | adapter | Bus impl: redb-backed topic store with cursors |
| `sturn-config` | adapter | ConfigSource port + scarab-config-file impl: sturn.{yaml,yml,toml} discovery |
| `sturn-dotenv` | adapter | Secrets impl: KEY=VAL file, chmod 600 |
| `sturn-fuse` | adapter | FUSE impl: mount a ws tree read-only for POSIX tools |
| `sturn-git` | adapter | Vcs impl via the git binary + WAL->commit snap |
| `sturn-keyring` | adapter | Secrets impl: secret-tool (libsecret) |
| `sturn-odb` | adapter | Direct git ODB access: loose objects, refs, trees — no process spawns |
| `sturn-systemd` | adapter | Service impl + deploy helpers: systemd user units |
| `sturn-wal-git` | adapter | Wal impl: ops as commits on refs/sturn/wal/\* via git plumbing |
| `sturn-ws-git` | adapter | Ws impl: read/list/materialize via git plumbing |
| `sturn` | engine | sturn — ephemeral coordination engine: claims/ops/topics over VCS state (engine lib + compat bin) |
| `sturn-driver` | driver | tamias-driver-sturn — pavo view driver over a repo's sturn coordination state plus engine ops dispatching to the sturn lib |

Rustdoc: `/api/sturn_core/` etc. after `bun run docs:api`.

# Explanation

* [Architecture](architecture.md) — the three layers, invariants, boundaries, where sturn sits
* [Boundaries](boundaries.md) — owns / doesn't-own, neighbors named
* [Concepts](concepts.md) — the domain vocabulary, defined once
* [Decisions](decisions.md) — ADR-lite: decision → alternative → consequence
* [The model — files, approval, agents](model.md) — virtual trees, per-op review
* [Why no CRDT for code](no-crdt.md) — convergence for the log, decisions for the tree
